key_insight: A coupled thermo-mechanical FEM model predicts AA6061 rotary friction welding behavior and quantitatively links simulated fields to experimentally measured microstructural zone boundaries.
engineering_relevance: The model supports welding-process optimization with less reliance on costly physical trials.
method: Axisymmetric ABAQUS/Standard model using coupled CGAX4HT elements.
Temperature-dependent material properties and high-temperature true stress–strain data.
Correlate predicted thermo-mechanical fields with DRZ, TMAZ, and HAZ boundaries.
evidence_signal: Predicted weld morphology, temperature evolution, and axial shortening agreed with experiments; joint characterization included microscopy, hardness, tensile testing, XRD, and SEM.
watch_item: The abstract reports no numerical prediction errors or validation range, leaving accuracy across other welding conditions uncertain.
paper_title: Thermo-Mechanical Modeling and Microstructural Evolution in Rotary Friction Welding of AA6061 Aluminum Alloy
